newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-ELS HOLDS THREE-STROKE LEAD AT BUICK.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELS HOLDS THREE-STROKE LEAD AT BUICK.

text.p: U.S. Open champion Ernie Els stood one round away from a second successive wire-to-wire win at the Buick Classic after shooting a four-under-par 67 at Westchester Country Club Saturday.
The South African had a three-day total of 14-under-par 199 and the same three-stroke lead he entered the third round with.

Closest to Els was a familiar contender. Jeff Maggert finished second to Els here last year and was one of the four contenders last Sunday for the U.S. Open title at Congressional. Maggert shot a 66 on Saturday.

Last year Els won here by eight strokes, and after 12 holes of the third round this year was already eight strokes ahead of the field. But Els lost two strokes coming in, and Maggert picked up three more over the last five holes. The two will play the final round together.

Jim Furyk, who finished fifth at Congressional last week, slipped from second to third place at Westchester after a 69 put him at nine under, five behind Els. Rookie Robert Damron stood alone in fourth place at eight under after a 68.
Els looked uncatchable after he birdied two of the hardest holes on the golf course, chipping in on the 11th and sinking a five footer on the 12th to get to 16 under par.
The bogeys came from a bad tee shot into the deep rough on 13, and a failure to get up and down from a bunker on 16.

"It's not too often you get a lead like that, but in the end shooting 67 isn't bad. I'm sure Jeff will come out aggressive tomorrow, but if I play sensibly, the way I have all week, I'll be okay," said Els.
Maggert started with a bogey on the first hole, but had six other birdies in the rest of the round.

"It was nice to finish the way I did. I made a little run at Ernie. It will be a good battle tomorrow. I've got a chance to win, but I have to make some birdies. Ernie is still in the driver's seat," said Maggert.

Maggert has said that he has never been more motivated to win than he is this week -- the direct result of what he described as the worst half hour of his career, the horrible multi-putt finish on the last two greens at Congressional.
The question that will be answered on Sunday is whether all the motivation Maggert can muster is enough to overcome the talent of Els and the momentum he brings from his U.S. Open win.
Tiger Woods birdied the last two holes to shoot an even-par round of 71 on Saturday. He has now had just one round under par in his last three tournaments.
"It's a little frustrating because I'm not playing as well as I should be, but that's going to happen, that's part of the game of golf," said Woods.

"The more you play, the more bad starts you're going to have, that's the way it is. It's just a matter of getting through it, though I can see a light at the end of the tunnel. I'm not saying I'm playing horrible, because I'm not, but I'm just not getting the most out of my game."
